description.value: The study investigated posterior cingulate cortex activation during a heroin-cue-reactivity task and resting-state functional connectivity differences between heroin users and healthy controls, including associations with duration of heroin use.

spans.text: The purpose of our study was to identify the PCC that was significantly activated during a cue-induced craving task.

value: The heroin group showed significantly greater activation in the bilateral posterior cingulate cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, caudate, putamen, precuneus, and thalamus during exposure to heroin-related cues compared with neutral cues and the healthy group (P < 0.001, uncorrected).
The increased posterior cingulate cortex activity in heroin users upon exposure to drug cues suggests that the PCC is involved in neurocircuits linked to reward and addiction cravings.
